successors.name: Spanish Empire
successors.text: Maynila, declared the Spanish city of Manila on 24 June 1571

ledger.x: c. 1500: Maynila is founded on the south bank of the Pasig. 'Manila was probably founded as a Bornean trading colony about 1500' (infobox: 'Establishment of Maynila and conversion to Islam: c. 1500'). Brunei's 'political influence over Maynila is not considered to have extended to military or political rule'.

c. 1520: Tondo presses on Maynila's territory. Ache's cousin, ruler of Tondo, was 'slyly' taking over 'territory belonging to Maynila' while Ache's mother ruled; infobox 'Death of Rajah Salalila and territorial conflicts with Tondo: c. before 1521'. Year bridged from 'before 1521'; where the border ran is not stated.
c. 1521: the conflict is over by the time Ache rules (c. 1521-1572); the page gives no treaty or last battle, so the year is a bridge.
May 1570: Martin de Goiti attacks Maynila.
1571: Maynila ends as an independent polity.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Maynila (Battle of Maynila)
wars.outcome: Goiti's May 1570 attack burned the settlement; in 1571 Legazpi allied with Lakandula of Tondo, the rulers of Maynila made a deal that let Spain claim the city, Bangkusay (3 June 1571) ended local resistance, and Manila was declared a Spanish city on 24 June…

wars.name: Maynila-Tondo territorial conflict
wars.outcome: No result recorded; the dispute predates Ache's rule (c.

certainty.note: A single walled bayan on the Pasig; no frontier is recorded, and Maynila's hinterland and the Tondo border are not given.
